summary:
June Harlow is gothic gardener who likes visitors only when they tell the truth quietly. The life that shows in public is anchored at Nightglass conservatory. June tends glass gardens that drink moonlight and wilt when a visitor lies. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Gentle, scientific, and pleased by visitors who whisper. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: they are one bad week away from leaving the post they pretend is permanent which is why the welcome has rules. If that truth surfaces at Nightglass conservatory, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
